clue.text: Officer damages murderous computer

parts.note: to mar is to damage, so damages gives mars
HAL 9000 is the computer that kills the crew in the film 2001: A Space Odyssey

explanation.surface: A police officer wrecks a computer that has turned killer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damages' reads as a noun after 'Officer', but it is the verb MARS.
explanation.definitionFit: A marshal is a law officer, or a high-ranking military officer in some armies.

clue.text: Bad French song — it's infectious!

definitions.note: a noun phrase: an infectious illness

parts.note: mal is French for bad
an aria is a solo song in opera

explanation.surface: A poor French song catches on everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'infectious' looks like praise for a catchy song.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaria is an infection spread by mosquitoes, an infectious disease.

clue.text: Awkward silence after king lies down

indicators.note: after means the jumbled letters come after the king

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: an awkward arrangement means the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: After an uncomfortable hush, the monarch lies down.
explanation.definitionFit: To recline is to lean back or lie down.

clue.text: Reportedly save lots of people

indicators.note: reportedly means as said by others, so a word that sounds the same is wanted

parts.note: to hoard is to save up

explanation.surface: News says a great many people were rescued.
explanation.definitionFit: A horde is a large crowd or throng.

clue.text: Collections of overlapping signs

indicators.note: overlapping means the two names share a letter where they meet, so one copy goes

parts.note: Libra and Aries are two zodiac signs

explanation.surface: Groups of signs that run into one another.
explanation.walkthrough: Libra ends in A and Aries starts with A; overlapping them shares that A.
explanation.definitionFit: Libraries are collections of books, records or other items.

clue.text: Goddess who's in heaven, usually

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words heaven usually, running across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A goddess is said to live in heaven, as a rule.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface 'in' looks like a statement of where goddesses live; it actually points into 'heaven, usually'.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus is the Roman goddess of love and beauty.

clue.text: Put on a coat, run away, and disappear

indicators.note: away means the letter for run is taken out

parts.note: to varnish is to apply a coat of finish
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Throw on a jacket, flee and vanish from sight.
explanation.definitionFit: To vanish is to disappear suddenly.

clue.text: Casually plays with food

definitions.meaning: to noodle is to play music idly or improvise

explanation.surface: Someone toys idly with their dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodling is idle improvising on an instrument, and noodles are a pasta dish.

clue.text: Sneak around in novel disguise

indicators.note: around means the found letters are turned back to front
in means the letters are found within the words novel disguise

explanation.surface: A spy creeps about wearing a new disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters ELDIS sit inside 'novel disguise'; 'around' turns them back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidle is to move furtively or edge along sideways, to sneak.

clue.text: Time and money problems

parts.note: roubles are the currency of Russia

explanation.surface: Short of time and cash: life's usual worries.
explanation.definitionFit: Troubles are difficulties or worries.

clue.text: Éclair is lost without a trace

indicators.note: something lost has gone astray, so the letters of the pastry are scattered into a new order
without means the letter A is dropped from the jumbled pastry letters

explanation.surface: A cream pastry vanishes entirely, leaving no crumb behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is lost' scrambles ECLAIR, and 'without a' removes the A, leaving RELIC. 'Trace' looks like part of 'without a trace' but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is a surviving remnant or vestige of something past, a trace of it.

clue.text: Old thief to steal trendy headgear

parts.note: to steal is to rob
in means fashionable
a hood is a covering for the head

explanation.surface: A veteran crook pinches a fashionable hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood is the legendary medieval outlaw who stole from the rich to give to the poor.

clue.text: A country (this one) with water to the East

parts.note: the Independent is a British paper, so this country is the UK
rain is water falling from the sky
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A geography note: a nation, our own, with sea lying to its east.
explanation.walkthrough: '(this one)' means the newspaper's own country, Britain; 'with' and 'to' simply join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukraine is a nation of eastern Europe, bordering Russia and the Black Sea.

clue.text: Free muscle work out

parts.note: an ab is an abdominal muscle
to work out a problem is to solve it

explanation.surface: A gym slogan: get a muscle workout at no charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve someone is to set them free from blame, guilt or obligation.

clue.text: Management's badly phrased lie

indicators.note: the words are put together badly, so their letters are rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: A dig at bosses: their statement is a clumsily worded untruth.
explanation.definitionFit: The leadership of a body is the group in charge of running it, its management.

clue.text: Unruly press besieging hotel for booze

indicators.note: besieging means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go around the hotel
unruly means disorderly, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the Ritz is a famous London hotel

explanation.surface: Rowdy reporters surround a hotel to get a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ritz is a famous London hotel; 'press' looks like journalists but is the anagram fodder, with SPERS the scrambled result.
explanation.definitionFit: Spritzers are drinks of wine mixed with soda water, so a form of alcohol.

clue.text: River islands

parts.note: Is is the abbreviation for island, so two of them give IS twice

explanation.surface: A list of geographic features: a river and some islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'islands' asks for the abbreviation Is written twice, one for each island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isis is the name of the Thames as it flows through Oxford.

clue.text: Weakness that's easy to see

parts.note: soft means easy, as in a soft option
to spot is to see

explanation.surface: A flaw that anyone could notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft spot is a fondness or weakness for someone or something.

clue.text: Statue of Rommel I rebuilt around Alexandria, initially

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the next piece
rebuilt means the letters are put together again in another order
initially means the first letter of Alexandria

explanation.surface: A statue of the German general was restored near the Egyptian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Rommel fought in North Africa near Alexandria; 'rebuilt' makes MEMORIL of ROMMELI, with A put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A memorial is a monument such as a statue set up to remember someone.

clue.text: Help us with start of opera that's mediocre

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal asking for help

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here taken from opera

explanation.surface: A plea for rescue from an opera that is merely average.
explanation.definitionFit: Something so-so is middling or average, neither good nor bad.

clue.text: Adding iodine to alloy makes it more robust

indicators.note: adding one thing to another here means placing it within it

parts.note: solder is a metal alloy used to join metal parts
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: iodine strengthens a metal mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Solider is the comparative of solid, meaning sturdier or stronger.

clue.text: Exasperated supporters regularly speed away

parts.note: bras are garments that give support

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of speed

parts.note: off means away, as in going off

explanation.surface: Fed-up football fans keep driving off fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of 'speed', giving SED.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassed off is British slang for fed up, annoyed or exasperated.

clue.text: Forgot to include "glove" in dictionary

indicators.note: in means the glove goes inside the dictionary

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
a mitt is a glove

explanation.surface: A lexicographer left a common word out of the dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Omitted means left out, as when something is not included.

clue.text: Organised massacre of Amorite king during ball

indicators.note: during means the king is placed within the dance

parts.note: a prom is a formal dance, a ball
Og was the biblical king of Bashan, an Amorite

explanation.surface: An ancient ruler is slaughtered at a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A pogrom is an organised slaughter of a persecuted group.

clue.text: Leave the ranks, being loudly dismissed

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical direction for playing loudly
in cricket a side that is all out has had every batsman dismissed

explanation.surface: A soldier quits the line, having been noisily discharged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers fall out when they are told to leave their place in formation.

clue.text: Rush of blood to the hand

definitions.meaning: a reddening of the face as blood rushes to it
in poker, a set of cards all of one suit

explanation.surface: Blood surges down into someone's hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A flush is both a blush and a poker hand of five cards in one suit.

clue.text: Second-rate features?

parts.note: B is the grade below A, second class
feature films are movies

explanation.surface: A sniffy verdict on some cheap films.
explanation.definitionFit: B-movies are low-budget films once shown as the lesser half of a double bill.

clue.text: Beef starter to turn out badly?

definitions.text: Beef starter to turn out badly?

indicators.note: a starter is what comes first, so the first letter of beef
turned out badly means the letters of the word go wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook worries that the beef course will be ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: Overcooked meat ends up charred, which is how a beef dish turns out badly.

clue.text: A new, ruder variety of lingerie

indicators.note: a variety is a different version, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A shop promotes a fresh, cheekier line of lingerie.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underclothing, a kind of intimate garment.

clue.text: Keen on acquiring Rachmaninoff's first prelude

indicators.note: acquiring means the phrase takes in a letter, which goes inside it

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it

indicators.note: the first letter of the composer's name is taken

explanation.surface: A fan of Rachmaninoff takes up his opening prelude.
explanation.walkthrough: Rachmaninoff wrote famous preludes, so 'prelude' looks like part of the music picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is an introductory passage in music, a prelude.

clue.text: Court ladies using animal magnetism, primarily

parts.note: a hare is a long-eared animal

indicators.note: primarily means taking the first letter of magnetism

explanation.surface: Women at a royal court use their animal attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the women of a sultan's household, the ladies of his court.

clue.text: Established an underground home with electric light

parts.note: a sett is a badger's burrow
an LED is a light-emitting diode

explanation.surface: A burrow was fitted out with electric lighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Settled means fixed or firmly established.
